title: Turn-aware soft-priority aging and slab compaction for continuous batching with mixed lengths
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Tune the continuous batching scheduler to improve latency and throughput for mixed prompt/response workloads by introducing 'turn-aware soft-priority aging' and a GPU-side slab compaction flow for KV cache. Focus on reducing KV fragmentation and improving slot coalescing for interleaved short and long turns while keeping tail latency SLOs intact.
background: Current continuous-batcher tends to fragment GPU KV caches when requests mix very short prompts with long responses (chat-style). Fragmentation increases memory pressure, forces early eviction of useful KV state, and reduces effective batch coalescing because short-turn slots are preemptively prioritized. Previous work addressed slot coalescing and KV heuristics (see ENG-314159) but we still see 12-18% throughput loss on heavy-mix traffic in prod-like traces. We need a scheduler-level policy that gracefully decays artificial priority on short turns and a compaction/defragmentation mechanism that reclaims GPU memory without causing large latency spikes.
proposed_solution: 1) Soft-priority aging: attach a per-turn soft-priority score that decays exponentially (configurable half-life) instead of hard timeouts. Short turns start with higher immediate priority to maintain latency but their score decays so they can be coalesced later if they remain waiting. 2) Turn-cohort coalescing: group slots into short/medium/long cohorts and allow constrained cross-cohort coalescing windows when occupancy is low. 3) GPU slab compaction: periodic lightweight compaction on the KV slab that migrates low-recently-used KV entries into a compressed region (quantized pointers) to free contiguous slabs for large KV allocations. Compaction is rate-limited and piggybacks on idle GPU epochs to avoid interfering with hot inference. 4) Prefetch advisory: use a length-prediction hint from the API to pre-reserve KV space for expected long responses to reduce mid-generation evictions.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end P50 latency for mixed workloads must not regress by >5% compared to baseline (no policy).
Tail P99 latency must remain within current SLO (baseline P99 + 8ms).
Throughput (tokens/sec) improves by >=6% on synthetic heavy-mix trace and does not drop by >2% on homogeneous long-only trace.
KV fragmentation metric (free contiguous slab ratio) improves by >=20% after compaction runs.
No user-visible errors or increased OOM incidents in staged environment during 72h soak.
Feature is toggleable via runtime flag and default-off for existing Dedicated customers until rollout is complete.

open_questions: What default half-life provides best balance for US-EAST production traces? (25ms vs 100ms)
Is GPU-to-GPU slab migration necessary or can compaction be local to a single device?
Should compaction be tenant-scoped (per-tenant slab) or global within a node?
What are worst-case latencies when compaction runs concurrently with long-turn generation?
Do we need to expose length-prediction hint in the public API or keep it internal-only?
Any impact on token accounting or billing when compaction compresses KV entries?
notes: Early perf runs: 2025-06-18 synthetic run showed 11% throughput gain and 19% contiguous-slab improvement with aggressive compaction (70% threshold) but a 6ms P99 increase in a minority of nodes under hot load.

Trade-offs: aggressive compaction reduces fragmentation but can add jitter; conservative compaction keeps latency stable but leaves fragmentation higher. We should ship conservative defaults and let perf team tune per-region.
Observation: many short turns are re-issued within 120ms windows; soft-aging with 50ms half-life allows them to be coalesced post-wait without hurting immediate latency.
Memory model: compacted region stores 8-bit quantized pointers and small LRU sketch for recency; prototype implemented in CUDA with async streams.
Interlocks: ensure compaction never moves KV state needed for an in-flight token generation. We use a per-slot pin counter to prevent migration while pinned.
Similar tickets: ENG-314159 (continuous-batcher-length-drift-mitigation) and ENG-42109 (decongestion-driven-continuous-batcher). Link them in dependencies.
